title: The Medallion Fund (Renaissance Technologies)
html:
What it is: the flagship fund of Renaissance Technologies, founded by mathematician Jim Simons in 1982. Medallion launched in 1988 and is widely considered the best track record in investing history.

The numbers

MeasureFigure
Average annual return, 1988–2018about 66% before fees, 39% after fees
2020+76%, while Renaissance's funds open to outside investors lost money
Who can investRenaissance employees only; closed to outsiders for about two decades
Sizekept small (reported around $10B); profits are paid out instead of letting it grow
Feesreported at 5% of assets plus 44% of profits — and still the best net returns around

Sources: Realtid (citing returns and outflows), The Man Who Solved the Market (Gregory Zuckerman).

How it works

  • Thousands of small, short-term statistical signals — patterns in price, volume and other data that repeat slightly more often than chance.
  • A tiny edge, repeated constantly. The firm's own people have described being right only a little over half the time. The money comes from making that edge pay across a huge number of trades, with leverage.
  • Scientists, not traders. Mathematicians, physicists and computer scientists — very few Wall Street hires.
  • No human overrides. If the model says trade, they trade.
  • Obsessive data cleaning and testing. A signal must prove itself on historical data before it's used.

Why outsiders couldn't copy it

Renaissance's outside funds (RIEF, RIDA, RIDGE) — run by the same firm — did far worse and lost about two-thirds of their outside money after 2020. The edge works only at limited size and very short holding periods.

What we borrow

  1. An edge is measured, not felt. Every setup we use goes through a test like the edge study.
  2. Small edges need many trades and strict sizing. One big bet on a "sure thing" is the opposite of Medallion.
  3. Rules before emotion. Write the plan before the trade (Trade Plan Template).
  4. Medallion wouldn't trust Fibonacci because it looks good on a chart. It would test it. So do we.
